headword: {二兎|にと}を{追|お}う{者|もの}は{一兎|いっと}をも{得|え}ず
reading: にとをおうものはいっとをもえず
gloss: he who chases two hares catches neither; don't try to do two things at once

definitions.gloss: if you try to do two things at once, you will fail at both
definitions.explanation: A proverb warning against spreading one's efforts too thin. By pursuing two goals simultaneously, you risk achieving neither.

examples.japanese: {二兎|にと}を{追|お}う{者|もの}は{一兎|いっと}をも{得|え}ずだ⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧。
examples.english: You know what they say — chase two rabbits and you'll catch neither.

examples.japanese: ⟦{仕事|しごと}→仕事：00480_shigoto⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{趣味|しゅみ}→趣味：00889_shumi⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{両方|りょうほう}→両方：01750_ryouhou⟧⟦やろう→やる：02980_yaru⟧⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧、{二兎|にと}を{追|お}う{者|もの}は{一兎|いっと}をも{得|え}ずになった。
examples.english: I tried to pursue both work and hobbies and ended up failing at both.

examples.japanese: {二兎|にと}を{追|お}う{者|もの}は{一兎|いっと}をも{得|え}ず⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧、⟦まず→まず：00796_mazu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{一|ひと}つ→一つ：02948_hitotsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{集中|しゅうちゅう}しよう→集中する：21908_shuuchuusuru⟧。
examples.english: Since they say chasing two hares gets you neither, let's focus on one thing first.

notes:
A well-known Japanese proverb derived from a Latin saying ("Duos qui sequitur lepores neutrum capit"). It warns against dividing one's attention between multiple goals, as doing so often leads to failure in all of them.

USAGE:
Typically used as advice or admonition when someone is trying to take on too much at once. Often followed by ⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧ or だ⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧ when quoting the proverb. Can also be used as a noun-like phrase to describe a situation: {二兎|にと}⟦{追|お}い→追う：02016_ou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧.

SIMILAR PROVERBS:
- ⟦{虻蜂取|あぶはちと}らず→虻蜂取らず：06293_abuhachitorazu⟧: trying to catch both a horsefly and a bee, catching neither — nearly identical meaning
- ⟦{一石二鳥|いっせきにちょう}→一石二鳥：04764_issekinichou⟧: killing two birds with one stone — opposite meaning (successfully achieving two goals at once)

CULTURAL NOTE:
This proverb is commonly used in business, education, and everyday advice contexts. The word {兎|と}/⟦{兎|うさぎ}→兎：01854_usagi⟧ (rabbit/hare) appears in several Japanese proverbs and idioms.
